StWillibrord Educational Trust is seeking an experienced, proactive Headmistress for its prestigious school campus in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

Key Responsibilities:
* Section Leadership: Direct academic and administrative functions of the school section (Primary/Middle wing), ensuring adherence to ICSE / board standards.
* Instructional Supervision: Review weekly lesson plans, observe classroom instruction, and coach teachers on effective instructional delivery.
* Student Wellbeing & Discipline: Supervise student attendance, code of conduct, counseling support, and pastoral care programs.
* Event & Activity Planning: Coordinate annual days, cultural celebrations, science fairs, sports tournaments, and literary competitions.
* Parent Communication: Conduct parent-teacher meetings, resolve parent feedback empathetically, and foster community trust.
* Examination & Reporting: Supervise the scheduling, conduct, and grading of periodic assessments and term-end examinations.

Qualifications & Requirements:
* Master's or Bachelor's degree with B.Ed. from an NCTE-recognized institution.
* Minimum 7 to 10 years of successful teaching experience with at least 3 years in academic coordination, supervisory, or headmistress roles in a reputed school.
* Outstanding leadership, conflict-resolution, and organizational skills.
* Exceptional verbal and written English communication.

The Heritage School, Vasant Kunj, invites applications from qualified and dedicated educators for the position of Trained Graduate Teacher (TGT) – Social Science, with a postgraduate qualification in Economics.

* Ability to promote critical thinking, collaboration and independent learning.

*Experience*

Relevant teaching experience in Social Science or Economics at the middle or secondary school level is preferred.

The roles and responsibilities of a school teacher can vary depending on grade level, subject, and school policies, but here are some common core duties and expectations:

*Instructional Planning*: Teachers are responsible for designing and delivering effective lesson plans that align with curriculum standards. They must adapt their teaching methods to accommodate diverse learning styles and abilities.

*Classroom Management*: Maintaining a positive and orderly classroom environment is crucial. Teachers must establish rules and expectations, manage student behavior, and address any disruptions that may arise.

*Assessment and Evaluation*: Teachers assess student performance through various means such as tests, quizzes, projects, and assignments. They analyze and use assessment data to track student progress and adjust instruction as needed.

*Curriculum Development*: In addition to lesson planning, teachers may have a role in developing or revising curriculum materials to meet the needs of their students and keep up with educational standards.

*Individualized Instruction*: Recognizing that students have different learning needs, teachers should provide additional support or challenges as required. This includes working with students who have special needs or require differentiated instruction.

*Communication*: Teachers communicate regularly with students, parents, and colleagues. They provide feedback on student progress, discuss concerns, and attend parent-teacher conferences and meetings.

*Professional Development*: Continuous learning is essential for teachers. They should engage in ongoing professional development to stay current with educational trends, teaching methods, and subject matter.

*Supervision and Safety*: Ensuring the safety and well-being of students is a top priority. Teachers must supervise students in and outside of the classroom and follow safety protocols.

*Collaboration*: Teachers often work as part of a team, collaborating with other educators, specialists, and support staff to address the diverse needs of their students.

*Counseling and Support*: Teachers sometimes act as mentors and provide emotional support to students who may be facing challenges at home or in their personal lives.

*Record-Keeping*: Maintaining accurate records of student attendance, grades, and other relevant information is essential for monitoring progress and complying with administrative requirements.

*Professional Ethics*: Teachers are expected to adhere to a code of professional ethics, which includes respecting student confidentiality, maintaining appropriate boundaries, and upholding the values of fairness and equity in their teaching practices.

*Community Involvement*: Engaging with the local community and participating in school events, clubs, or extracurricular activities can be part of a teacher's responsibilities.

*Technology Integration*: In today's digital age, teachers are often expected to incorporate technology into their teaching methods and use it for communication and instructional purposes.

*Cultural Sensitivity*: Being aware of and respecting cultural and diversity issues in the classroom is crucial for creating an inclusive learning environment.

Senior SDET – Automation Framework Architect (Playwright, Selenium, API, CI/CD)
THE ROLE

Own test strategy, quality architecture, and the automated regression infrastructure for Securly Flex — the flex period scheduling and attendance platform that 1,000+ schools use every school day to place students into intervention, enrichment, and support sessions.

Flex decides where students are supposed to be. A defect in Autoassign placement, capacity limits, separation rules, roster sync, or attendance recording does not just break a feature — it can put a student in the wrong room, leave a must-attend intervention empty, place students together who are required to be kept apart, or send inaccurate attendance into a district's student information system. The test infrastructure you build is the last line of defense before production.

This is an engineering leadership role, not a QA role. You will define what "production-ready" means for Flex, build the automation platform that enforces it through CI/CD quality gates, and write production-quality code for that platform yourself. You will also serve as the team's expert on rules-engine correctness and edge-case testing — your understanding of how Flex's rules interact (priorities, capacity limits, restricted sessions, sign-up cutoffs, and check-in controls) directly shapes both the test suite and the implementation team's design decisions.

Location: Pune, India (Hybrid – 2 days onsite)
Experience: 6–10+ years
Reports to: Director of Quality Engineering

WHAT YOU'LL DO
Own the quality bar. Define what "passing" means for Flex: establish written quality criteria covering scheduling correctness, data integrity, access control, and performance that gate production releases.
Test the rules engine. Design and implement automated test suites covering Autoassign placement logic — student choice, teacher priority, must-attend assignments, rostered and restricted sessions, at-risk designations, seat and room capacity, separation (contact control) rules, conflict detection, and the guarantee that manual registrations are never overwritten — plus the edge cases around them: conflicting rules, boundary conditions, concurrent registrations at capacity limits and sign-up cutoffs, API calls that skip UI validation, and permission boundaries.
Gate every release. Build CI/CD quality gates that prevent regressions from reaching production; own the pipeline configuration and ensure the quality bar is enforced, not advisory.
Set performance baselines. Measure and establish written performance baselines for peak-load moments: sign-up windows opening and closing, Autoassign runs before each flex period, and attendance taking across thousands of concurrent users; define the thresholds that constitute a performance regression.
Cover web, mobile, and integrations. Own end-to-end coverage across web, mobile, and integrations: student, teacher, and admin workflows; the student mobile app; email, in-product, and push notifications; roster imports and attendance exports to the SIS; and the shared rostering and single sign-on Flex runs on with Securly Pass.
Build the framework. Architect and build the Flex automation framework: reusable libraries, test data utilities for roster and attendance files, parallel execution, and reporting that the whole team extends — and contribute fixes to product code where it improves testability.
Mentor and scale. Mentor engineers on test architecture as a first-class discipline, and bring AI-assisted tooling into how the team generates scenarios, triages failures, and scales coverage.
Shape architecture. Partner with your technical lead and the Distinguished Engineer on architecture and testability decisions, and influence testing standards across teams beyond your own squad.
Own incidents. Join the on-call rotation and own the full incident lifecycle for quality regressions: detection, diagnosis, resolution, and retrospective.

SKILLS & REQUIREMENTS
Must-Have
Test framework architecture — designing automation frameworks from scratch (page object or screenplay patterns, BDD where it fits, parallel execution, reporting) that other engineers extend. You build the platform, not just the scripts.
Test automation (SDET-level) — Playwright, Cypress, or Selenium for UI plus API-level automation (REST, contract testing). Must automate business-rule behavior — placement decisions, capacity and eligibility rules, state transitions — not just UI interaction tests.
CI/CD quality gates — integrating test suites into pipelines; defining and enforcing regression gates for a multi-tenant product used daily by 1,000+ schools. At this level you own the definition of the bar, not just the tests that check it.
Rules-engine and data-integrity testing — designing deterministic test data and fixtures for scheduling, allocation, or eligibility logic; building data utilities that validate rosters, registrations, and attendance across CSV/XML imports, exports, and concurrent edits.
Strong programming — JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or Python at production quality (TypeScript strongly preferred). Your test code is held to the same review standard as product code.
Technical communication — ability to produce written quality criteria, test strategy and edge-case documentation, and performance baseline documents that the implementation team, engineering manager, PM, Support, and leadership can act on.
Education & experience — Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related technical field, with 6 to 10+ years of hands-on SDET / test automation experience.
Strongly Preferred
Performance & concurrency testing — k6, JMeter, Gatling, or Locust; modeling burst traffic (thousands of users acting in the same minute) and catching race conditions at capacity limits and sign-up cutoffs.
AI-assisted test engineering — using AI tools to generate test scenarios, triage failures, or scale framework adoption across teams.
Security & access-control testing — role-based permissions (student / teacher / admin), multi-tenant data isolation between districts, and student data privacy expectations.
Nice to Have
Mobile test automation — Appium, Maestro, Detox, or similar for iOS and Android; push notification and device-fragmentation coverage.
Integration testing — SIS data import/export, rostering sync, single sign-on, and notification delivery (email, in-product, push).
K-12 EdTech domain — understanding of bell schedules, flex and advisory periods, MTSS intervention tiers, and how districts manage SIS data helps design realistic test scenarios.
WHO YOU ARE
You test the edge cases, not just the happy path. You test the ways the system should fail and doesn't, and you document those cases so the implementation team designs against them.
You have built automation frameworks from the ground up — not just inherited them — and other engineers have built on what you designed.
You treat test architecture as a first-class engineering discipline. A feature without a regression suite is not finished — and you enforce that standard through CI/CD gates, not just code review comments.
You define what "quality" means on a product that decides where students are supposed to be, and produce written criteria that hold the codebase to that standard across every engineer and every release.
You are hands-on at a senior level — you still write the framework code, and you raise the bar for everyone who writes tests after you. Experience shipping product feature code is a bonus, not a requirement.
Your edge-case documentation and performance baselines are used by the implementation team to make better architecture decisions. Your influence extends past your own work.
You own your area end to end with minimal oversight, and you resolve ambiguity in requirements and design tradeoffs instead of waiting for a fully formed spec.

Tech Giant Scale. EdTech Innovation. Unmatched Student Impact.

Securly processes over 1.1 billion requests per day and 54 TB of data daily, protecting more than 20 million students across 20,000+ schools globally. Since pioneering the first cloud-based web filter for K–12 in 2013, Securly has built one of the most trusted, high-scale platforms for student safety, wellness, and engagement.

By turning data into meaningful, actionable intelligence, Securly enables schools to identify risk earlier, reduce harmful incidents, and strengthen student support — driving measurable improvements in student safety and wellbeing at scale.

About Kotak Education Foundation
Kotak Education Foundation (KEF) works towards improving the quality of education by strengthening teachers, school leaders and education systems.
We are looking for experienced Consultant Trainers to deliver high-quality teacher training programmes across Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat.

Role Purpose
The Consultant Trainer will be responsible for facilitating high-quality, engaging and practice-oriented training programmes for teachers and education stakeholders across the assigned state.
The ideal candidate should have a strong foundation in teacher education and classroom pedagogy, with relevant experience in at least one of the following domains:
Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN)
English Language Learning and Acquisition
Pedagogy
Use of Technology in Education
The role also requires the ability to contextualise training to the language, curriculum and classroom realities of the respective state.

Deliver face-to-face and, where required, virtual training programmes for teachers and education stakeholders.
Facilitate training sessions using participatory, experiential and activity-based methodologies.
Conduct demonstrations, modelling sessions, practice activities, teach-backs and reflection sessions.
Create an environment that encourages teacher participation, discussion and application.
Adapt facilitation approaches based on participant profiles, school contexts and learning needs.
Support teachers in translating training concepts into classroom practice.
2. Domain Expertise
The Consultant Trainer should have demonstrated experience in at least one of the following domains:
A. Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN)
Foundational literacy and numeracy concepts and classroom practices.
Early-grade language and mathematics pedagogy.
Play-based, activity-based and experiential approaches.
Reading, writing, oral language and foundational mathematics.
Classroom assessment and identification of learning gaps.
Familiarity with NIPUN Bharat / foundational learning objectives will be an advantage.

English language teaching and language acquisition.
Teaching English in multilingual classroom contexts.
Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing (LSRW).
Communicative language teaching and learner-centred pedagogy.
Vocabulary, grammar and reading development.
Understanding of language acquisition principles.
Familiarity with CEFR or other language proficiency frameworks will be an advantage.
C. Pedagogy
Strong understanding of effective teaching-learning practices.
Learner-centred and activity-based pedagogy.
Experiential and inquiry-based learning.
Differentiated instruction and inclusive classroom practices.
Lesson planning, classroom management and assessment.
Ability to translate pedagogical theories into practical classroom strategies.
D. Use of Technology in Education
Integration of technology into teaching and learning.
Digital pedagogy and technology-enabled classroom practices.
Use of digital tools and platforms for teaching, learning and assessment.
Ability to demonstrate technology tools to teachers with varying levels of digital proficiency.
Familiarity with AI-enabled educational tools will be an advantage.
3. Training Preparation & Design
Study training manuals, facilitator guides, presentations and supporting resources before delivery.
Prepare for training through dry runs, practice and self-learning.
Provide feedback on training materials based on field experience.
Adapt examples and activities to local classroom contexts without compromising programme objectives.
Support the CCT team in developing or refining training resources when required.

Travel extensively within the assigned state to conduct teacher training programmes.
Work across urban, semi-urban and rural locations as required.
Coordinate with project teams, school leaders and field teams to ensure smooth training delivery.
Maintain professional conduct and represent KEF appropriately at partner and beneficiary locations.
Demonstrate flexibility regarding training locations, schedules and participant groups.

Maintain accurate records of trainings conducted, participant attendance and training-related data.
Complete training reports and feedback documentation within stipulated timelines.
Collect and communicate field-level observations, challenges and success stories.
Use participant feedback and observation data to improve subsequent training delivery.
Adhere to KEF's training quality standards and processes.
